newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch central bank wants to control esoteric funds.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central bank wants to control esoteric funds.

text.p: The Dutch Central Bank wants tighter controls on some of the more esoteric new investment funds -- such as those investing in teak, diamonds and ostriches -- but has not yet decided how to go about this.
"We want to get more of a grip on funds which are not under (our) supervision," spokesman Jan-Paul Altes told Reuters on Tuesday, adding that no clear process for doing this had yet been formulated.
Dutch media has this week reported that the Central Bank plans to launch a test case against one teak fund which, under existing regulations, does not come under its supervision.
In something of a legal loophole, the bank only supervises investment funds with a collective investment strategy.
Funds of an individual nature -- where investors buy a share of a whole investment project, such as one square metre of teak trees -- can operate outside bank supervision.
Newspapers said the bank would begin proceedings soon against the Bosque Teca Verde teak fund to see if it had contravened existing laws.
"We have not taken a decision on any official step," Altes said, adding that it would be wrong to conclude that all funds not supervised by the Central Bank were breaking the law.
Altes said the Central Bank currently supervised almost 350 investment funds in the Netherlands, but he could not quantify how many funds were working outside the bank's supervision.
On Monday, Dutch daily de Volkskrant named the Albeco Diamond Fund and the Ostrich Farming Corporation as unsupervised funds that had recently failed.
The Dutch Shareholders' Association (VEB) said it welcomed the Central Bank move as several new funds hold out the prospect of huge returns for some investors.
